'''''Ageratum conyzoides''''' ('''billygoat-weed''', '''chick weed''', '''goatweed''', '''whiteweed''', '''mentrasto''') is native to Tropical America, especially [[Brazil]], and is an [[invasive species|invasive weed]] in many other regions. It is an herb that is 0.5–1 m. high, with ovate leaves 2–6 cm long, and flowers are white to mauve.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Ageratum conyzoides'' |work=NSW Flora Online |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Ageratum~conyzoides }}</ref>

In [[Vietnamese language|Vietnamese]], the plant is called ''cứt lợn'' (meaning "pig feces") due to its growth in dirty areas.<ref>[[:vi:Cứt lợn]]</ref>

==Uses==
As a [[medicinal plant]], ''Ageratum conyzoides'' is widely used by many traditional cultures against [[dysentery]] and [[diarrhea]].<ref name="PandaLuyten2018">{{cite journal|last1=Panda|first1=Sujogya Kumar|last2=Luyten|first2=Walter|title=Antiparasitic activity in Asteraceae with special attention to ethnobotanical use by the tribes of Odisha, India|journal=Parasite|volume=25|year=2018|pages=10|issn=1776-1042|doi=10.1051/parasite/2018008|doi-access=free|pmid=29528842|pmc=5847338|url=}} </ref>  It is also an [[insecticide]] and [[nematicide]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Ming |first=L.C. |chapter=''Ageratum conyzoides'': A tropical source of medicinal and agricultural products |chapter-url=http://www.hort.purdue.edu/newcrop/proceedings1999/v4-469.html |editor-first=J. |editor-last=Janick |title=Perspectives on new crops and new uses |publisher=ASHS Press |location=Alexandria VA |year=1999 |isbn=978-0961502706 |pages=469–473 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NR1IAAAAYAAJ}}</ref><ref name="PandaLuyten2018"/>

==Toxicity==
Ingesting ''A. conyzoides'' can cause [[liver]] [[lesions]] and [[tumors]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Sani, Y. |author2=Bahri, S. |title=Pathological changes in liver due to the toxicity of Ageratum conyzoides |journal=Penyakit Hewan |volume=26 |issue=48 |pages=64–70 |year=1994 |url=http://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search/display.do?f=1997/ID/ID97008.xml;ID9600846 |issn=0216-7662 |access-date=2013-08-31 |archive-date=2023-04-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423162058/https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search/display.do?f=1997/ID/ID97008.xml;ID9600846 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Fu, P.P. |author2=Yang, Y.C. |author3=Xia, Q. |author4=Chou, M.C. |author5=Cui, Y.Y. |author6=Lin G. |title=Pyrrolizidine alkaloids-tumorigenic components in Chinese herbal medicines and dietary supplements |journal=Journal of Food and Drug Analysis |volume=10 |issue=4 |pages=198–211 |year=2002 |url=http://www.fda.gov.tw/files/publish_periodical/10-4-1.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120105233916/http://www.fda.gov.tw/files/publish_periodical/10-4-1.PDF |archive-date=2012-01-05 }}</ref> There was a mass poisoning incident in Ethiopia as a result of contamination of grain with ''A. conyzoides''.<ref>{{cite journal |author =Wiedenfeld, H. |title=Plants containing pyrrolizidine alkaloids: toxicity and problems. |journal=Food Additives & Contaminants: Part A |volume=28 |issue=3 |pages=282–292 |year=2011 |doi=10.1080/19440049.2010.541288  |doi-access=free|pmid=21360374 |s2cid=23218347 |url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00673672 }}</ref> The plant contains the [[pyrrolizidine alkaloids]] [[lycopsamine]] and [[echinatine]].

==Weed risk==
''A. conyzoides'' is prone to becoming a rampant environmental [[weed]] when grown outside of its natural range. It is an invasive weed in Africa, Australia, Southeast Asia, Hawaii, and the USA.<ref>[http://www.hear.org/gcw/species/ageratum_conyzoides/ Global Compendium of Weeds, Ageratum conyzoides (Asteraceae)]</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.herbarium.unc.edu/flora.htm | title = Flora of the Carolinas, Virginia, and Georgia, and Surrounding Areas | author = Alan S. Weakley | date = April 2008 | access-date = 2009-03-05 | archive-date = 2018-10-06 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20181006082209/http://herbarium.unc.edu/flora.htm | url-status = dead }}</ref> It is considered a moderate weed of rice cultivation in Asia.<ref>{{cite book |first=B.P. |last=Caton |title=A Practical Field Guide to Weeds of Rice in Asia |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ver3qCQF9EEC |year=2004 |publisher=Int. Rice Res. Inst. |pages=16–17  |isbn=978-971-22-0191-2}}</ref>
